The United Church of God (UCG) is a denomination of Christianity. It is one of many denominations to come out of the Worldwide Church of God (WCG) in 1995. The Worldwide Church of God was started by Herbert W. Armstrong. UCG calls itself "The United Church of God, an International Association", with the last three words italicized. This is so people do not confuse it with other churches. UCG is its own denomination. After Herbert Armstrong's death in 1986, leaders in the WCG began to change the teachings of the church. This started in 1994. They changed the teachings to be more like other Christian churches. Many of the members wished to keep the original teachings, which they believed were the same beliefs as the early church of the First Century. Because of this, they left to start their own churches. UCG was established in May 1995 and is the largest church to come out of the WCG. UCG began when former WCG ministers met in Indianapolis, Indiana in the spring of 1995. The were concerned about the changing teachings of the church. UCG's first president was David Hulme. He was later removed from office because he refused to move the church's home office to Ohio in 1998, among other reasons. After this, he left to start a new church called "Church of God, an International Community." After Hulme, the Council of Elders elected new presidents. They elected Les McCullough in 1998, Roy Holladay in 2002, Clyde Kilough in 2005, Dennis Luker in 2010, and Victor Kubik in 2013. Rick Shabi was elected president in 2022. UCG is led by twelve men called the "Council of Elders". They are elected by a group of church ministers called the "General Conference of Elders." This is not like the WCG, which was led by one man only. The General Conference of Elders meets once a year in May to decide how money should be spent and how the church should be run. They also decide the teachings of the church and go to seminars. The council meets four times a year. UCG's "Home Office" and is in Milford, Ohio, (a suburb of Cincinnati). This office is led by UCG's president, who is also the church's main spokesperson. He also leads the church's ministers and controls the printing of the church magazine, newsletter, and booklets. He is elected by the Council of Elders (COE) and can be removed by them. The UCG believes and worships like many other Christian churches, except: UCG believes that some Christian beliefs have been wrongly changed long ago in the early church. It believes they were changed by people who tried to mix their own ideas with Christian beliefs. It believes they did this because they hated Jews, or were pagan, or Gnostics, or Greek philosophers. These wrong ideas became traditions in the Catholic church and Protestant churches, which they believe go against the teachings of the Bible. So, for example, they don't worship holidays that started out as pagan, like Halloween, Christmas, Valentine's Day, and New Year's Day. UCG does not believe in the Trinity. It believes that this was also a wrong idea that was later mixed into the teaching of the Bible. Instead, it believes that the Bible teaches that the Holy Spirit is the spirit/power of God and of Christ Jesus and is not a separate person. They believe that God "the Father" and Jesus Christ are two separate beings in the "God Family". UCG believes that Christians are begotten as children in the "Family of God", and after they die, at the return of Christ, they will be resurrected as spirit beings who are like God and will rule the universe with God as part of His family. UCG believes Jesus Christ's main message was about the Kingdom he was coming to establish on earth to rule over all the nations. UCG believes that Christians will not go to heaven when they die, but will live and rule forever with Jesus Christ on earth. Later, they will also rule the universe with Jesus as part of the "God Family". UCG also believes that sinners who do not repent will not go to Hell, but will be simply be destroyed by God. It believes that the idea of "Hell", as some teach it, is not really in the Bible. UCG believes that the people of Western Europe (and early settlers of the United States) are from the Ten Lost Tribes of the northern kingdom of ancient Israel. It also believes that Jews today come from the ancient southern kingdom of Judah. They do not believe this because they believe that some races are better or worse than others, but because they believe there are prophecies about the United States and Europe in the Bible. UCG believes that many laws in the Old Testament should be obeyed by Christians today, such as the Ten Commandments. They believe that certain foods such as pork and shellfish should not be eaten by Christians. They also believe the Holy Day festivals in the Old Testament should also be kept by Christians, including the "Days of Unleavened Bread", and the "Feast of Tabernacles". They also believe in observing the Sabbath on Saturday (from Friday sunset to Saturday sunset), and that Christians should not commit sexual sins. They do not believe in obeying the laws in the Old Testament about sacrifice, because they believe these laws were "fulfilled by the sacrifice of Christ." UCG believes that people who do not know or really understand the truth of the Bible during their life will be given time to learn after a "Second Resurrection" to a new physical life, living again during the Millennium in God's Kingdom. If they still reject God's Holy Spirit and way of life, God will destroy them after the "Third Resurrection" along with former believers who had also rejected God. They are destroyed in the third resurrection (the "resurrection of fire") in the Lake of Fire, along with Satan and his demons. UCG teaches that members should give 10 percent of their income to the church to fund the gospel mission. Members are also taught to save a Second tithe, or another 10 percent for them to use themselves to observe festivals like the Feast of Tabernacles. Ambassador Bible College (ABC) is an in-depth nine-month program where students can learn about the Bible, Christian living and the teachings of the United Church of God. The program also prepares young people to lead and serve, and it prepares them to teach future generations. Students study church teaching and all the books of the Bible thoroughly. UCG states: "The mission of the Church of God is to preach the gospel of Jesus Christ and the Kingdom of God in all the world, make disciples in all nations and care for those disciples." Their goal is to preach about "The Kingdom of God" to everyone, through the UCG website, through Twitter and YouTube, and through radio, magazines, booklets, and television. Beyond Today magazine is UCG's main publication. It is a free magazine and is published every two months. The magazine contains articles about Bible prophecy, world news, church teachings and Christian living. The Beyond Today Television Program appears on WGN America and on the WORD Network and on 28 Public-access television cable TV stations. It also includes a multimedia website and a channel on YouTube and on Roku. Vertical Thought appears four times a year for young people, and appears on the internet only. It contains articles from both ministers and young people in the church. The United News is a newsletter about news within the United Church of God. It also includes articles about Christian living, and news about the death of church members, and births in their families. UCG also has 33 booklets on different Bible teachings, and a 12-lesson Bible study course. It also has a monthly Bible reading program where the Bible is explained, and a number of articles. Kingdom of God Bible seminars began in September 2011 and are held at different locations around the world.

The United Church of Canada is the largest Protestant Christian denomination in Canada, and the second largest Canadian Christian denomination after the Roman Catholic Church. It was started in 1925 when four Canadian churches decided to merge: the Methodist Church of Canada, the Congregational Union of Ontario and Quebec, two-thirds of the congregations of the Presbyterian Church in Canada, and the Association of Local Union Churches. In 1968, the Canadian branch of the Evangelical United Brethren Church decided to join the United Church of Canada.
United First Parish Church, Quincy, Massachusetts is a Unitarian Universalist church in Quincy, Massachusetts. It became the parish church of Quincy in 1639. The building was built in 1828.

The United Methodist Church of Sweden was a Christian denomination in Sweden. It existed between 1868 and 2012. It contributed towards the creation of the Uniting Church in Sweden. According to a report from 2009, the denomination had 6,436 members.

The United Methodist Church (UMC) is a Methodist–Christian denomination that is one of the largest Protestant churches in the United States. It was founded in 1968 by the union of the Methodist Church (USA) and the Evangelical United Brethren Church. The UMC traces its roots back to the teachings of John and Charles Wesley in England. With over 8 million members and 35,000 churches it is second only to the Southern Baptist Convention among Protestant denominations. As of 2009, worldwide membership was about 12 million. It is a member of the World Council of Churches, the World Methodist Council, and other religious associations.

The United Nations Partition Plan for Palestine was a plan approved by the United Nations on 29 November 1947. It proposed dividing Mandatory Palestine, then under British rule, into two countries: one Jewish and one Arab. Jerusalem would not belong to either state but would be controlled internationally. Jewish leaders accepted the plan because it supported the creation of a Jewish state, later established as the State of Israel in 1948. Arab leaders rejected the plan because they opposed dividing the land. This disagreement was one of the reasons for the outbreak of the war in 1948 and became a key-point in the Israeli-Palestinian conflict. From 1517 to 1917, Palestine was part of the Ottoman Empire. Most people living there were Arab Muslims and Christians, with a small Jewish minority in cities like Jerusalem, Hebron, Safed, and Tiberias. People usually identified with their religion, their town, or the Ottoman state, not with a separate Palestinian nation. In the late 1800s, the Zionist movement in Europe began supporting Jewish immigration to Palestine. Some Arab leaders opposed this immigration and asked the Ottoman government to stop land sales to Jewish settlers. The Ottoman authorities tried to control immigration, but they did not fully prevent it. By the early 1900s, tensions between Arab residents and Jewish immigrants were increasing. During World War I, Britain and France secretly signed the Sykes-Picot Agreement, which planned how to divide parts of the Middle East after the defeat of the Ottoman Empire. After the war, Britain took control of Palestine. In 1917, Britain also issued the Balfoure Declaration, supporting the creation of a Jewish “national home” in Palestine. In 1922, the League of Nations officially gave Britain the Mandate for Palestine. During this time, Jewish immigration increased, especially in the 1930s when many Jews fled persecution in Europe to Israel because of the rise of antisemitism. By the 1930s and 1940s, violence in Palestine increased. Arab groups opposed Jewish immigration, and Jewish armed groups also carried out attacks. Britain tried to control the situation, but fighting and unrest continued. After World War II, Britain found it too difficult and costly to keep control. In 1947, Britain decided it could no longer control the situation in Palestine because of increasing violence and asked the United Nations (UN) to decide what should happen next. The UN created a special group called the United Nations Special Committee on Palestine (UNSCOP). This group studied the situation and suggested dividing Palestine into two states, one Jewish and one Arab, and suggested that Jerusalem should be controlled internationally. On 29 November 1947, the UN General Assembly voted in favor of this plan.The plan was approved with 33 countries voting in favor, 13 against, and 10 abstaining. Countries such as the United States and the Soviet Union supported the plan. Many Western countries also voted in favor. Most Arab and Muslim countries voted against the plan because they believed it was unfair to the Arab population in Palestine. Major world powers played an important role in the vote on the Partition Plan. The United States strongly supported the plan and encouraged other countries to vote in favor.The Soviet Union also supported the plan, which was unusual because the two countries often disagreed during this period. Britain, which controlled Palestine at the time, did not support the plan. Instead, it chose to abstain from the vote and focused on ending its rule in the region. The support of both the United States and the Soviet Union helped the plan gain enough votes to pass in the United Nations. However, the lack of British support made it harder to implement the plan on the ground. The United Nations Partition Plan of 1947 was not the first plan to divide Palestine. In 1937, a British group called the Peel Commission suggested dividing the land into a Jewish state and an Arab state, giving less land to the Jewish state and more to the Arab population. However, both Jewish and Arab leaders rejected this earlier plan, although some Jewish leaders were willing to discuss it. By 1947, the situation had changed. There were more Jewish immigrants, and tensions had increased. The UN plan gave more land to the Jewish state and included international control of Jerusalem. Unlike the earlier plan, the UN proposal was accepted by Jewish leaders but rejected by Arab leaders. The UN Partition Plan suggested splitting Palestine into two states, one for Jews and one for Arabs, while Jerusalem would be controlled by the United Nations. Both states would share trade and resources in an economic union, and each state would handle its own security and police. The plan aimed to give both groups their own country while keeping Jerusalem neutral. At the time of the UN Partition Plan, Palestine had a mixed population of Jews and Arabs. Most Arabs lived in rural areas, villages, and small towns, while many Jews lived in cities and along the coastal areas. Important cities like Jerusalem and Haifa had both Jewish and Arab populations. The population was not clearly separated. In many parts of the country, Jews and Arabs lived close to each other, making it difficult to draw clear borders between the two proposed states. The United Nations tried to divide the land based on where each group lived, but the result was complex. The Jewish state would include areas with large Arab populations, and the Arab state would include some Jewish communities. This created concerns about minorities living in both states. The plan gave about 55% of the land to the Jewish state and about 45% to the Arab state although Jews were a smaller part of the total population. The Jewish state included much of the coastal region and some desert areas, while the Arab state included hill regions and parts of the countryside. The UN Partition Plan included an economic union between the Jewish and Arab states. This meant that the two states would be separate, but still work together in some economic areas. They would share resources like water, roads, and railways. Trade between the two states would be open, so goods could move easily across borders. The Jewish state included much of the coast and important ports, which helped with trade, while the Arab state had more farmland, which was important for agriculture. The plan was meant to help both states grow and stay stable, but the conflict and lack of trust made it difficult for for this cooperation to work in reality. The United Nations Partition Plan was adopted as a resolution by the UN General Assembly in 1947, making it an official decision of the United Nations, known as Resolution 181. However, UN resolutions are not legally binding, meaning they are recommendations but not laws that countries or groups are required to follow. Therefore, while The United Nations adopted the Partition Plan as a resolution, it did not have the power to enforce it. The UN Partition Plan was made to try to stop the fighting between Jews and Arabs in Palestine and aimed to give both groups their own independent states. Jerusalem was to be managed by the United Nations so that all religious groups could access its holy sites safely. The plan also hoped the two states would work together economically, sharing trade, resources, and transport. Another goal was to help each state create local governments and security forces to keep order. Overall, the plan’s intention was to offer a peaceful solution to a long-standing conflict, even though the UN knew this would be difficult to achieve. The reactions to the Partition Plan were very different among Jews and Arabs in Palestine. Most Jewish communities accepted the plan, even though some disagreed with the borders. They saw it as an important step toward creating their own state. In contrast, most Arab communities strongly rejected the plan. They believed it was unfair, especially because the Jewish state was given more land while Arabs made up a larger part of the population. After the UN vote, there were celebrations in many Jewish areas, while protests and strikes took place in Arab communities. Tensions quickly increased, and violence between the two groups began soon after the announcement of the plan. These different reactions made cooperation between the two sides almost impossible and contributed to the outbreak of conflict. The plan was met with disapproval in Arab nations. Mass demonstrations against the plan erupted in cities, buildings belonging to Europeans were vandalised and damaged, and some called for Jihad. In some Arab states, Jews became targets of violence and were injured or killed. Jewish homes, schools and businesses were also targeted and destroyed. The Arab League met to discuss their response to the partition. Member states agreed to provide weapons, training and funding to Palestinian Arabs. However, they were unwilling to send their own armies to intervene in Palestine as they wanted to avoid a conflict with the British. The United Nations Palestine Commission (UNPC) was created to help carry out the Partition Plan. Its task was to gradually take control of Palestine from the British support the creation of the two new states. The commission comprised of five members from different countries: Chairman Karel Lisicky (Czechoslovakia), co-chair Raul Diaz de Medina (Bolivia), Morgan Per Federspiel (Denmark), Eduardo Morgan (Panama) and Vicente J. Francisco (Philippines). Britain refused to fully cooperate and did not allow the Commission to take real authority on the ground before their withdrawal. At the same time, the Commission needed cooperation from both Jewish and Palestinian leaders. However, the Palestinian Arab leadership boycotted the process, while Jewish representatives attempted to gain the favour of the UNPC. The UN Partition Plan created two states, but the populations were mixed. This meant that both states would include large minority groups. This raised concerns about how these minorities would be treated. The plan included ideas to protect minority rights, such as equal rights and protection of property and religion. However, because of the high level of tension and lack of trust, many people doubted that these protections would work in practice. The presence of large minority groups made the division more complicated and increased fears on both sides. At the time of the Partition Plan, the security situation in Palestine was unstable. There was already violence between Jewish and Arab groups, and both sides had armed organizations. Jewish groups had more organized militias, such as the Haganah, which were prepared to defend Jewish areas. Arab groups also had fighters, but they were less organized at the local level. The United Nations did not have its own army to enforce the plan or keep peace between the two sides. Britain was also preparing to leave and did not want to stay involved in the conflict. Because there was no strong authority to maintain order, violence increased quickly after the plan was announced. This made it very difficult to carry out the plan peacefully. After the UN voted in favor of the Partition Plan in 1947, violence between Jewish and Arab groups quickly increased. This period is often called the civil war in Mandatory Palestine. Fighting broke out in cities, towns, and along roads. Both sides attacked each other’s communities and transport routes. Many people were forced to leave their homes because of the violence. The situation became more serious as both sides tried to gain control over important areas before the end of British rule. This conflict continued until 1948, when a larger war began after the creation of Israel. The UN Partition Plan was never fully carried out. In May 1948, Jewish leaders declared the creation of the State of Israel, based partly on the ideas of the plan. Soon after, several neighboring Arab countries, including Egypt, Jordan, Syria, and Iraq, attacked Israel. This led to the Arab-Israeli War of 1948. The war ended with the signing of the Rhodes Armistice in 1949. During the war, Israel gained control of 78% of Palestinian mandate, more land than it had been given in the UN plan. The Arab state that was proposed in the plan was never created. Instead, Jordan took control of the West Bank, and Egypt took control of the Gaza Strip. The war also caused a large refugee crisis. Hundreds of thousands of Palestinians fled or were forced to leave their homes. Many of them moved to nearby countries or to other parts of Palestine. At the same time, many Jewish people moved to the new state of Israel, including refugees from Europe and the Middle East. These events had long-lasting effects. The failure of the Partition Plan and the war that followed would shape the future political situation in the region. Jerusalem was given a special international status in the UN Partition Plan. It was not meant to be part of either the Jewish or Arab state. Instead, the United Nations planned to control the city directly. This was because Jerusalem is important to three major Abrahamic religions; Judaism, Christianity, and Islam. The goal was to protect the holy sites and allow free access for all religious groups. The city and its surrounding area were meant to become an international zone, separate from both states. However, this plan was never fully implemented. During the war in 1948, Jerusalem was divided into two parts. West Jerusalem came under Israeli control, while East Jerusalem was controlled by Jordan. Jerusalem has remained a central issue in the conflict ever since. Both Israelis and Palestinians claim the city as their capital, and its final status is still disputed today. The Palestine issue shaped the relationship between Israel and its neighbours for many years. Relations were poor in the years following the war and multiple military conflicts occurred. On June 5, 1967, following increasing tensions in the region, Israel attacked Egypt, leading to what is known today as the Six Day War. By the end of the conflict, Israeli forces occupied Egyptian, Syrian and Palestinian territories. On 6 October 1973, Egypt and Syria attacked Israel leading to the October War. Israel, with the help of the United States, was able to repel the attack, and a ceasefire was signed on October 24. Egypt was the first Arab state to normalise relations with Israel following the 1978 Camp David accords, a move that angered the other Arab nations and led to Egypt's expulsion from the Arab league. Since then, some Arab nations have gradually normalised relations with Israel. Today, Egypt, Jordan, the United Arab Emirates, Morocco, Bahrain and Sudan recognise Israel. Nonetheless, the Palestine issue continues to be a point of disagreement. The UN Partition Plan had a strong and lasting impact on the Israeli-Palestinian conflict. It introduced the idea of dividing the land into two separate states, which later became known as the “two-state solution.” Even though the plan was never fully carried out, it influenced many later peace efforts. International organizations and governments have often returned to the idea of two states living side by side. Many of the problems that existed in 1947 are still important today. These include disagreements over borders, the status of Jerusalem, and the rights of Palestinian refugees. Because of this, the Partition Plan is still discussed in politics and diplomacy. It is often seen as an early attempt to solve a complex conflict that remains unresolved. The most recent attempt at a two state solution was the 2025 United Nations resolution 80/72 on the Settlement of the Question of Palestine, a proposed framework for resolving the Gaza War which included a two state solution. The UN Partition Plan is considered a key moment in modern history. It was one of the first major actions taken by the United Nations to try to solve an international conflict. The plan played an important role in the creation of the State of Israel in 1948. At the same time, it marked the beginning of a long and difficult conflict between Israelis and Palestinians. It also showed both the possibilities and the limits of international organizations. While the UN was able to create a plan, it was not able to enforce it or prevent violence. Historians have different opinions about the UN Partition Plan. Some believe it was a fair and necessary solution at the time, given the growing conflict and the need to find a political answer. Other historians argue that the plan was unfair, especially to the Arab population, because it gave more land to the Jewish state even though Jews were a smaller part of the population. They also say the plan did not fully take into account the realities on the ground. Historians also focused on different aspects of the plan. Some historians focus on the role of the United Nations and major powers, such as the United States and the Soviet Union, in supporting the plan. Others focus more on the experiences of local people and how the plan affected their lives. Because the conflict is still ongoing, different perspectives continue to influence how the plan is understood. This makes it an important and debated topic in both history and politics.

The United Presbyterian Church in the United States of America (UPCUSA) was the largest branch of Presbyterianism in the United States from May 28, 1958, to 1983. It was formed by the union of the Presbyterian Church in the United States of America (PCUSA) with the United Presbyterian Church of North America (UPCNA) in Pittsburgh Pennsylvania, in May 1958. In 1983, the vote was finally held regarding the merger, with a unanimous 151 presbyteries in the UPCUSA affirming it, and the PCUS affirming it 53 to 8. On June 10, 1983, the first General Assembly was held for the new denomination, which would be called the Presbyterian Church (USA).

The United States Conference of Catholic Bishops (USCCB) is the episcopal conference of the Catholic Church in the United States. It was founded in 1966 as the joint National Conference of Catholic Bishops (NCCB) and United States Catholic Conference (USCC). It is made up of all active and retired members of the Catholic hierarchy (i.e., diocesan, coadjutor, and auxiliary bishops and the ordinary of the Personal Ordinariate of the Chair of Saint Peter) in the United States and the Territory of the U.S. Virgin Islands., the president is Los Angeles's archbishop, Archbishop José Horacio Gómez.

The United States Commission on International Religious Freedom (USCIRF) is part of the U.S. government. It was made by a law called the International Religious Freedom Act (IRFA) in 1998. The people in charge of USCIRF are chosen by the President and leaders from both political parties in the Senate and House of Representatives. USCIRF's main job is to check facts about religious freedom problems in other countries and give advice to the President, the Secretary of State, and Congress on what to do.

The Uniting Church in Sweden is a Christian Protestant denomination in Sweden. It was established on 4 June 2011 out of the Baptist Union of Sweden, the United Methodist Church and the Mission Covenant Church of Sweden as the Joint Future Church. The name was changed during a conference in Karlstad on 11 May 2013.

A universal religion is a religion that tries to be inclusive and applicable to all people, regardless of their cultural, ethnic, or geographic background. It typically seeks to offer spiritual guidance, moral principles, and a sense of community to followers worldwide. Examples of religions that have been considered universal to some extent include Christianity, Islam, Buddhism, Hinduism, and Sikhism. These religions have many people who follow them and aim to provide guidance and spiritual fulfillment to people of different backgrounds.

Universidad de Santa Isabel, also called USI or Santa Isabel, is a Catholic private school ran by Sisters of Charity of Saint Vincent De Paul in Naga, Camarines Sur, Philippines. It was found by Rt Rev. Francisco Gainza, O.P., Bishop of Caceres. in 1868 as the first normal school for girls in the Philippine area named in credit of St. Isabel, Queen of Hungary. Colegio de Santa Isabel was founded by Rt Rev. Francisco Gainza. The management of the school gave to six Daughters of Charity that go to the Bicol Region of the Philippines. It was opened in September 18, 1870. Queen Isabella II of Spain allowed Don Fray Francisco Gainza, Bishop of Nueva Caceres. to make the school girls only which will be under the Daughters of Charity's care. This school was the first normal school only for girls in the Philippines and the Southeast Asia named Escuela Normal de Maestras. The school was opened April 12, 1868, achieved its university status in 2001, and got renamed to Universidad de Sta. Isabel. It is in Elias Angeles St., Bagumbayan Sur, Naga City. The University of Jamestown is a private Christian university in Jamestown, North Dakota, United States. It was started in 1883 by the Presbyterian Church. The school has about 1,300 students enrolled. It has always been co-educational. Until August 2013, the school was called Jamestown College. The University of Jamestown was started as Jamestown College in 1883. It closed during the depression of 1893. The school opened again in 1909. It has stayed open ever since. In 1979, Jamestown College's football team went to the NAIA National Championships. Two graduates have become Rhodes Scholars. In 2013, Jamestown College changed its name to the University of Jamestown. The Jamestown sports teams are called the Jimmies. The university is a member of the National Collegiate Athletic Association (NCAA). The Jimmies are members of the Northern Sun Intercollegiate Conference (NSIC). Three sports that the NSIC does not have play elsewhere—men's soccer and women's wrestling as independents, and men's volleyball in the Great Lakes Valley Conference. Previously, the Jimmies were members of the North Star Athletic Association (NSAA). They were members from 2013–14 to 2017–18, and again in 2024–25. The Jimmies previously played in the Great Plains Athletic Conference (GPAC) from 2018–19 to 2023–24, and in the Dakota Athletic Conference (DAC) from 2000–01 to 2011–12. They were also NAIA Independent within the Association of Independent Institutions (AII) during the 2012–13 school year. Jamestown plays in 24 sports: Men's sports include baseball, basketball, cross country, football, golf, ice hockey, soccer, track and field (indoor and outdoor), volleyball and wrestling; while women's sports include basketball, cross country, golf, ice hockey, soccer, softball, swimming & diving, track & field (indoor and outdoor), volleyball and wrestling; and co-ed sports include eSports and shotgun sports.
